# Results — Study 660 (Carry-Everywhere)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Koijen-Moskowitz-Pedersen-Vrugt (2018): **a carry signal predicts returns in every
major asset class, and a diversified cross-asset carry basket is a robust premium**.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint
`ed7c280e84fe`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes, 11 tickers (4,974 rows), 2007-06-01 → 2026-06-30, resampled to **228 month-end observations** 2007-07 → 2026-06 |
| Tickers | FX: `AUDUSD=X` `NZDUSD=X` `JPY=X` `CHF=X` · Bond: `IEF` `SHY` · Equity: `VYM` `VUG` · Commodity: `DBC` `GSG` · Cash reference: `BIL` |
| Sample start | 2007-06 — first full month after `BIL`'s 2007-05-30 inception (the binding constraint across all 11 tickers) |
| Construction | four **static** long/short sleeves, composition fixed *ex ante* (not a monthly-re-ranked signal — zero look-ahead, like a public calendar); monthly rebalance to par weights at each month-end close |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett) *t* for each sleeve's and the combo's one-sample mean; circular block-bootstrap (block=6mo, 2,000 draws) 95% CI on the combo Sharpe; skew; max drawdown |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: monthly rebalance to par weights at month-end close (no signal-formation lag — the basket never changes); one-way cost × first-order rebalance turnover per sleeve, plus a short-leg ETF borrow spread (EQ 40 bps/yr, CMD 25 bps/yr; FX/Treasury legs pay none — the carry proxy itself **is** the financing differential) |
| Data quirks (named) | all four sleeves are **transparent static proxies** — fixed textbook classification (AUD/NZD high-carry, JPY/CHF funding; IEF long/SHY short duration; VYM high-yield/VUG growth; DBC optimum-yield/GSG naive-roll) — not live deposit rates, a monthly-re-ranked G10 cross-section, or an actual futures term structure. No survivorship: all four legs are diversified index ETFs / spot FX, not single-name panels |

## The four sleeves — gross monthly carry legs

| sleeve | ann % | ann vol % | Sharpe | HAC *t* | skew | max DD % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **FX** (AUD+NZD / JPY+CHF) | −0.48 | 10.39 | −0.05 | **−0.20** | −0.74 | −39.60 |
| **BOND** (IEF / SHY) | +1.71 | 5.62 | +0.30 | **+1.33** | +0.23 | −20.82 |
| **EQ** (VYM / VUG) | −3.90 | 11.05 | −0.35 | **−1.44** | −0.07 | −60.71 |
| **CMD** (DBC / GSG) | +2.41 | 7.14 | +0.34 | **+1.39** | +0.75 | −23.99 |

None of the four legs individually clears **|t| ≥ 2**. The FX leg — the textbook
carry trade — is flat-to-negative over this window, consistent with the well-known
post-2008 zero-rate-era carry drought (echoed in [364-fx-carry-trade](../364-fx-carry-trade/)'s
own *t* = 1.14 on a longer, differently-weighted G10 basket — same direction, same
"literature-real, this-tape-thin" honesty). The equity-dividend leg is the most
damaging: VYM has lost outright to VUG over a period dominated by the mega-cap growth
bull market, a **secular value/growth divergence** the dividend-carry proxy cannot
distinguish from carry per se — named honestly, not laundered into the headline.

## Correlation matrix (monthly gross sleeve returns)

| | FX | BOND | EQ | CMD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **FX** | 1.00 | −0.24 | −0.11 | −0.26 |
| **BOND** | −0.24 | 1.00 | −0.06 | +0.30 |
| **EQ** | −0.11 | −0.06 | 1.00 | −0.05 |
| **CMD** | −0.26 | +0.30 | −0.05 | 1.00 |

The legs genuinely are close to uncorrelated (|ρ| ≤ 0.30) — KMPV's "loosely
correlated" premise holds structurally. It just doesn't help: diversification shrinks
the *volatility* around a mean, and here the mean is already indistinguishable from
zero.

| Sharpe | **−0.02** |

| skew | +0.01 |
| max drawdown | −18.51% (a slow multi-year bleed into 2025-10, not a single crash month) |

Statistically zero every way we cut it. The bootstrap CI straddles zero by a wide
margin — this is not "barely misses," it is "genuinely can't tell the sign."

## Robustness — alternate combo weightings

| construction | ann % | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| equal-weight, 4 sleeves (headline) | −0.07 | −0.02 | −0.08 |
| inverse-vol weight, 4 sleeves (FX 0.19 / BOND 0.35 / EQ 0.18 / CMD 0.28) | +0.48 | +0.14 | +0.62 |
| equal-weight, **ex-equity** 3 sleeves (FX+BOND+CMD) | +1.21 | +0.30 | **+1.41** |

Dropping the weakest (equity) leg and re-weighting both help the point estimate — but
even the best variant tried (ex-equity, 3 sleeves) tops out at *t* = 1.41, still short
of the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar. No construction choice rescues a `REAL` stamp on this tape.

## Costs — one-way rebalance cost × turnover + short-leg borrow

| | value |
|---|--:|
| avg monthly one-way turnover (frac of NAV) | FX 0.048 · BOND 0.018 · EQ 0.074 · CMD 0.091 |
| net at 5 bps one-way | ann **−0.26%**, Sharpe −0.07, HAC *t* = −0.31 |
| net at 10 bps one-way | ann **−0.30%**, Sharpe −0.08, HAC *t* = −0.35 |

An already-zero gross combo gets modestly *more* negative net of realistic costs —
turnover here is low (these are static baskets, rebalanced only to reset drift, not
re-ranked), so costs are not what kills the claim. There is simply no gross edge to
begin with.

## Third axis — does carry crash everywhere at once? (2008 GFC / 2020 COVID)

| window | combo cumulative | other-months mean/mo | FX | BOND | EQ | CMD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2008 GFC** (2008-08 → 2008-11, n=4) | **−0.96%** | −0.001% | **−27.09%** | +4.69% | +13.66% | +8.43% |
| **2020 COVID** (2020-02 → 2020-04, n=3) | **+2.26%** | −0.016% | −4.62% | +4.62% | **−10.68%** | **+20.87%** |

The folklore "carry crash" story is that every carry leg unwinds *together* the
moment risk appetite turns — that's the textbook argument for why carry earns a
premium at all (it's compensation for a tail you sell). It did not happen this way,
in either crisis, on this tape: in 2008 the FX leg (the classic AUD/JPY carry trade)
cratered **−27%** while bond, equity and commodity carry were all solidly *positive*
(equity-dividend value stocks outperformed growth in the GFC drawdown; Treasuries
rallied on flight-to-quality; DBC's optimum-yield roll held up better than GSG's
naive roll). In 2020 the equity leg cratered **−11%** (growth crushed value in the
recovery) while the commodity leg *spiked* **+21%** — GSG's heavier, naive front-month
crude exposure cratered harder than DBC's optimum-yield methodology during the
April-2020 negative-oil-price episode, blowing the roll-yield spread wide open. The
combo's actual worst stretch (max drawdown −18.5%) is a slow 2023-2025 bleed — mostly
the persistent equity-dividend leg losing to the AI-era growth rally — not a
crisis-month crash at all.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic synthetic four-sleeve world: independent Gaussian noise around a
TUNABLE planted carry mean, all four sleeves loaded on a shared TUNABLE
"synchronized-crash" factor that fires in ~5% of months; no network.

| world | Sharpe | HAC *t* | skew |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (no carry, no crash), **20 seeds** | — | mean **−0.15** (sd 1.13), \|t\|≥2 in **1/20** seeds | — |
| planted carry = +40 bps/mo, no crash (seed 660) | +0.56 | **+2.50** | +0.41 |
| planted carry = +40 bps/mo **with** a planted synchronized crash | −0.01 | **−0.06** | **−2.84** |

The detector doesn't fire on the null (1/20 seeds ≈ the expected 5% false-positive
rate for a two-sided test) and lights up cleanly on a planted premium alone
(*t* = 2.50). The third row is the honest, instructive one: bolting a *shared* crash
factor onto the *same* +40 bps/mo premium — with nothing else changed — drags the
HAC *t* back down to noise. It's a plausible mechanism for why a real cross-asset
carry premium *could* still fail to certify on any one 19-year tape: tail risk that
loads on all legs together, even occasionally, does more damage to a HAC *t* than a
same-sized idiosyncratic vol increase would. *(A faithful-engine / power check only —
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp; note the real 2008/2020 windows above
did NOT show this synchronized pattern, which is itself informative.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Equal-weight combo: **−0.07%/yr, Sharpe −0.02, HAC *t* = −0.08**,
  bootstrap 95% Sharpe CI **[−0.45, +0.43]**. No individual leg clears *t* ≥ 2 (best:
  commodity roll-yield *t* = 1.39); even the best alternate construction tried
  (ex-equity 3-sleeve) reaches only *t* = 1.41. The legs are genuinely close to
  uncorrelated (|ρ| ≤ 0.30) — but diversifying four means near zero still yields a
  mean near zero.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Nothing to harvest: net of costs and short-leg borrow the
  combo is **−0.26%/yr (5 bps) to −0.30%/yr (10 bps)**, Sharpe **−0.07 / −0.08**.
- **"Crashes everywhere at once?" — BUSTED.** In the 2008 GFC window the combo was
  roughly flat (**−0.96%**) because the FX leg's **−27%** carry unwind was offset by
  positive bond/equity/commodity carry; in COVID 2020 the combo was **+2.3%** because
  the equity leg's **−11%** slide was offset by the commodity leg's **+21%** spike.
  The individual legs *do* crash hard — just not on the same calendar, in this
  sample, which is exactly why the combo's mean stays near zero instead of
  going sharply negative.
